Analysis: Both hypotheses propose innovative, non‐invasive biomarker panels aimed at improving early HCC detection beyond AFP. Hypothesis 1 combines tumor-derived exosomal microRNA signatures with ctDNA methylation patterns, which leverages well-established techniques and a broader range of molecular indicators. This integration offers a plausible and testable framework through established assay methodologies and could improve sensitivity in AFP-negative patients once candidate markers are clearly defined and standardized. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 centers on exosomal TERT promoter methylation along with circulating microRNA profiles—a novel combination with sound biological rationale but less clarity on biomarker specificity, standardization, and mechanistic details. Both are safe diagnostics, but the overall feasibility and clarity in candidate selection and experimental design tips the balance in favor of Hypothesis 1.
